title: En or ett
description: Say a or an in Swedish with the right word, en or ett.

guide.summary: Every Swedish noun is either an en-word or an ett-word. Most are en-words; some endings tell you the group, and the common ett-words you learn by heart. The same split decides ingen or inget and någon or något.

sections.title: Two articles, and en is the big one
sections.text: Swedish has two words for a or an: en and ett. Every noun belongs to one group, and the article shows which. About three nouns in four are en-words, and words for people and animals are nearly all en-words.

rows: en man, en kvinna, en pojke, en bror
en bil, en bok, en stol
ett hus, ett bord, ett äpple

steps: Is the noun a person or an animal? Then take en.
Otherwise check the ending: some endings decide it.
If nothing helps and you do not know the word, guess en: you will be right three times in four.

examples.sv: Jag har en hund och en katt.
examples.en: I have a dog and a cat.

watch: Barn (child) is the famous exception: ett barn, even though it is a person.
Djur (animal) itself is an ett-word: ett djur.

sections.title: Endings that mean en
sections.text: Some endings settle the question. Nouns with these endings are en-words, so you can use the right article even for a word you have just met.

rows: en lärare, en läkare, en spelare
en flicka, en penna, en lampa

steps: Look at the end of the noun.
If it ends in -ning, -het, -else, -tion, -are or -a, take en.
Keep the article even when an adjective comes between: en bra lösning.
watch: A few -a nouns are ett-words, but they are rare at this level: ett öga, ett hjärta.
Nouns ending in -are are usually people, so two clues point to en.

sections.title: Endings that mean ett
sections.text: A few endings point to the smaller group. They are rarer, but when you see them, think ett.

rows: ett museum, ett gymnasium, ett centrum

steps: Check whether the noun ends in -um, -eri or -ande.
If it does, take ett.
For -ande, remember it is a strong hint rather than a rule; words for people in -ande are en-words.

examples.en: We are going to a museum.

watch: Words for people ending in -ande are en-words: en studerande.
Ett centrum stays centrum with the: centrum.

sections.title: Everyday ett-words to learn by heart
sections.text: Many short, common nouns are ett-words with no clue in their spelling. Learn each one with its article, as one unit: not hus, but ett hus.
steps: Ask yourself: is this one of the everyday ett-words?
If you learnt it as ett hus, ett bord and so on, use ett.
If the word is new, check the dictionary and learn it with its article.

examples.sv: Det står ett bord i köket.
examples.en: There is a table in the kitchen.

watch: The -e ending tells you nothing: ett äpple but en pojke.
An adjective after ett takes -t as well: ett litet land, ett stort hus.

sections.title: No and any follow the gender
sections.text: The words for no and some or any change like en and ett. The ett-word form ends in -t, just as ett does.
steps: Decide whether the noun is an en-word or an ett-word.
For an en-word use ingen or någon.
For an ett-word use the form with -t: inget or något.
watch: Inte någon and inte något mean the same as ingen and inget: Vi har inte någon bil.
Do not say inte en bil for no car; use ingen bil.

sections.title: No article for jobs and nationality
sections.text: When you say what someone is by job or nationality after är, Swedish uses the bare word with no en or ett, unlike English a or an.
steps: Is the sentence saying what someone works as, or where they are from, after är?
If so, leave the article out.
If an adjective stands before the job, put the article back: en bra läkare.
watch: Do not copy the English a: Han är läkare, not Han är en läkare.
The article returns with an adjective, and it follows the gender of the noun.

steps: Is the noun a person or an animal? Take en.
Remember the exceptions: ett barn, ett djur.
With no clue, en is the safe guess.
Look at the end of the noun.
-ning, -het, -else, -tion, -are and -a mean en.
Look at the end of the noun.
-um, -eri and usually -ande mean ett.
Recall whether you learnt the word with ett.
Hus, barn, äpple, bord, jobb, land and rum take ett.
Decide en-word or ett-word.
En-word: ingen, någon.
Ett-word: inget, något.
Is it a job or nationality after är? Drop the article.
Is there an adjective before the job? Put en or ett back.

mistakes.why: Ett belongs to the smaller group of nouns. Katt is an animal, and animals are almost always in the larger group.

exercises.hint: People and animals are almost always en-words.
exercises.feedback: Think about what kind of noun katt is.
exercises.explanation: Katt is an animal, and animals are nearly always en-words: en katt.

mistakes.why: Ett is the form for the smaller noun group. A woman is a person, and words for people almost always go with the other article.

exercises.feedback: People are almost always en-words.
exercises.explanation: Kvinna is a person, so it takes en: en kvinna.

mistakes.why: Ett goes with ett-words, and words for people are almost never ett-words.

exercises.feedback: When you are unsure, en is the safe bet, and for people it is nearly certain.
exercises.explanation: Pojke is a person, so it is an en-word: en pojke.

exercises.source: I have a dog and a cat.
answers: Jag har en hund och en katt.
Jag har ett hund och ett katt.
mistakes.why: Animals are almost always in the larger noun group, so ett is the wrong article for both.

answers: Jag har en hund och katt.
mistakes.why: In Swedish each noun normally keeps its own article.

exercises.feedback: Each noun needs its own article, and animals take en.
exercises.explanation: Hund and katt are animals, so both are en-words: en hund, en katt.

exercises.instruction: Replace barn with flicka and change the article to match. Write the whole sentence.

mistakes.why: The article still matches barn. Flicka is an en-word, so the two words now disagree.
That is the original sentence: barn was not replaced.

exercises.hint: Flicka is a person and ends in -a.
exercises.feedback: The article follows the new noun.
exercises.explanation: Barn is one of the few ett-words for people, but flicka is a normal en-word: en flicka.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. Bror is a person, so the ett-word article is the error.
A single countable noun like bror needs an article here.

exercises.feedback: Check the article in front of bror.
exercises.explanation: Bror is a person, and people are en-words: en bror.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence: I see a man. Leave one tile unused.

mistakes.why: That tile is the ett-word article, and words for people almost always take the other one.

exercises.feedback: Only one article fits a word for a person.
exercises.explanation: Man is a person, so it is an en-word: en man.

mistakes.why: Ett does not go with -ning. That ending belongs to the larger noun group every time.

exercises.feedback: Some endings give the gender away.
exercises.explanation: Nouns ending in -ning are always en-words: en tidning.

mistakes.why: Ett is for ett-words. The noun here ends in -ning, an ending that never takes ett.

exercises.hint: Look at the ending of lösning, not at bra.
exercises.feedback: The article agrees with the noun, even with an adjective in between.
exercises.explanation: Lösning ends in -ning, so it is an en-word: en bra lösning.

mistakes.why: Ett does not fit -tion. Nouns with that ending belong to the larger group.

exercises.feedback: Words ending in -tion form one group.
exercises.explanation: Nouns ending in -tion are en-words: en station.

mistakes.why: Nouns ending in -a are almost all en-words, so ett is wrong here.
One pen needs an article in front of it.

exercises.feedback: Most nouns ending in -a are en-words.
exercises.explanation: Penna ends in -a, so it is an en-word: en penna.

exercises.instruction: Replace bord with lampa and change the article to match. Write the whole sentence.

mistakes.why: The article still matches bord. Lampa ends in -a and belongs to the other group.
That is the original sentence: bord was not replaced.

exercises.feedback: The article belongs to the noun, so it changes with it.
exercises.explanation: Lampa ends in -a like flicka, so it is an en-word: en lampa.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. The -ning ending never takes ett, so the article is the error.

exercises.feedback: The ending tells you the article here.
exercises.explanation: Every noun ending in -ning is an en-word: en lösning.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence: A teacher is waiting. Leave one tile unused.

mistakes.why: That tile is the ett-word article. Nouns ending in -are are people, and they take the other article.

exercises.hint: Lärare ends in -are and is a person.
exercises.feedback: Two clues point the same way.
exercises.explanation: Nouns in -are are people who do something, and they are en-words: en lärare.

mistakes.why: Ett does not go with -else. Nouns with that ending are in the larger group.

exercises.feedback: The -else ending belongs to one group.
exercises.explanation: Nouns ending in -else are en-words: en händelse.

mistakes.why: En is the usual guess, but the -um ending points to the smaller group.

exercises.feedback: Some endings point to ett.
exercises.explanation: Nouns ending in -um are usually ett-words: ett museum.

mistakes.why: En is the default, but -eri is one of the endings that takes the other article.

exercises.feedback: The ending -eri is a clue.
exercises.explanation: Nouns ending in -eri are ett-words: ett bageri.

mistakes.why: En is the default, but nouns like this one, made from a verb with -ande, usually take the other article.

exercises.feedback: Nouns made from verbs with -ande are often ett-words.
exercises.explanation: Meddelande ends in -ande, a common ett-word ending: ett meddelande.

exercises.source: There is a bakery on the street.
answers: Det finns ett bageri på gatan.
Det ligger ett bageri på gatan.
Det finns en bageri på gatan.
Det ligger en bageri på gatan.
mistakes.why: Nouns ending in -eri take the smaller group article, not the default one.

exercises.feedback: Look at the ending of the word for bakery.
exercises.explanation: Bageri ends in -eri, so it is an ett-word: ett bageri.

exercises.instruction: Replace restaurang with museum and change the article to match. Write the whole sentence.

mistakes.why: The article still matches restaurang. Museum ends in -um and takes the other article.
That is the original sentence: restaurang was not replaced.

exercises.feedback: The article follows the new noun.
exercises.explanation: Museum ends in -um, so it is an ett-word: ett museum.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. The -um ending points to the smaller group, so the article is wrong.

exercises.feedback: The article does not fit the noun.
exercises.explanation: Museum ends in -um, so it takes ett: ett museum.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence: I got a message. Leave one tile unused.

mistakes.why: That tile is the default article, but nouns ending in -ande usually take the other one.

exercises.feedback: Look at the ending of the noun.
exercises.explanation: Meddelande ends in -ande, so it is an ett-word: ett meddelande.

mistakes.why: En is the default, but hus is one of the everyday words that belong to the smaller group.

exercises.hint: Hus is one of the everyday ett-words.
exercises.feedback: No ending helps here: you have to know the word.
exercises.explanation: Hus is a common ett-word to learn by heart: ett hus.

mistakes.why: En is the usual guess, but äpple belongs to the smaller group. Learn it with its article.

exercises.hint: Äpple is a word to know by heart.
exercises.feedback: The ending -e does not help; learn the article with the word.
exercises.explanation: Äpple is an ett-word: ett äpple.

mistakes.why: En is the default, but bord is a common word that takes the other article.

exercises.hint: Bord is one of the common ett-words.
exercises.feedback: You need to know this word with its article.
exercises.explanation: Bord is an ett-word: ett bord.

mistakes.why: Most words for people take en, but barn is an exception and takes the other article.

exercises.hint: Barn is an exception among people.
exercises.feedback: Most people are en-words, but not this one.
exercises.explanation: Barn is one of the few ett-words for people: ett barn.

exercises.instruction: Replace lägenhet with hus and change the article to match. Write the whole sentence.

mistakes.why: The article still matches lägenhet. Hus is in the other group, so the words disagree.
That is the original sentence: lägenhet was not replaced.

exercises.feedback: The article belongs to the new noun.
exercises.explanation: Lägenhet ends in -het and is an en-word, but hus is an ett-word: ett hus.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. Äpple belongs to the smaller group, so the article is wrong.

exercises.hint: Äpple is a word to know by heart.
exercises.feedback: Check the article in front of äpple.
exercises.explanation: Äpple is an ett-word: ett äpple.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence: I have a job. Leave one tile unused.

mistakes.why: That tile is the default article, but jobb is an everyday word from the smaller group.

exercises.feedback: Only one article fits jobb.
exercises.explanation: Jobb is an ett-word: ett jobb.

mistakes.why: En does not fit: land is an ett-word, and the adjective litet with its -t already shows that.

exercises.hint: Land is a common ett-word; litet agrees with it too.
exercises.feedback: The adjective already shows the gender with its -t.
exercises.explanation: Land is an ett-word, so it is ett litet land: both the article and the adjective show it.

mistakes.why: Inget is for ett-words, like inget hus. Bil is an en-word, so the -t form does not fit.

exercises.feedback: Ingen and inget follow the gender like en and ett.
exercises.explanation: Bil is an en-word (en bil), so no car is ingen bil.

mistakes.why: Någon goes with en-words. Bröd is an ett-word, so it needs the -t form.

exercises.feedback: Någon and något follow the gender like en and ett.
exercises.explanation: Bröd is an ett-word, so the question uses något bröd.

mistakes.why: Ingen is the en-word form. Kaffe is an ett-word, so it takes the form ending in -t.

exercises.feedback: The ett-word form ends in -t, like ett.
exercises.explanation: Kaffe is an ett-word, so no coffee is inget kaffe.

mistakes.why: Inget belongs with ett-words, and bil is an en-word.
Swedish says no car with a single word that follows the gender, not with inte and the article.

exercises.feedback: The word for no follows the gender of bil.
exercises.explanation: Bil is an en-word, so no car is ingen bil.

exercises.instruction: Make the sentence say I have no job, using ingen or inget. Write the whole sentence.

mistakes.why: Ingen is the en-word form, but jobb is an ett-word.
This keeps the article and adds inte, which is not how Swedish says no job.

exercises.feedback: Ett turns into the matching negative form.
exercises.explanation: Jobb is an ett-word, so ett jobb becomes inget jobb.

answers: Det finns inte något hotell här.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. Hotell is an ett-word, so the en-word form is the error.

exercises.feedback: The word for no must match the gender of hotell.
exercises.explanation: Hotell is an ett-word (ett hotell), so it takes inget.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence: Is there a bank here? Leave one tile unused.

mistakes.why: That tile is the ett-word form, but bank is an en-word.

exercises.feedback: Någon and något follow the gender.
exercises.explanation: Bank is an en-word, so the question uses någon bank.

mistakes.why: Inget goes with ett-words. Hund is an animal and an en-word.

exercises.hint: Hund is an animal, so an en-word.
exercises.feedback: Pick the form that matches en.
exercises.explanation: Hund is an en-word (en hund), so I see no dog is jag ser ingen hund.

mistakes.why: English says a teacher, but Swedish leaves out the article when saying what someone works as.
No article belongs here, and this noun is not an ett-word in any case.

exercises.feedback: After är, a job stands alone.
exercises.explanation: Swedish drops the article before a profession after är: hon är lärare.

mistakes.why: Svenska is the language, or the form for plural nouns. For one person's nationality use the plain adjective.
A nationality after är takes no article, and the ett-word article fits even less.

exercises.feedback: Nationality after är is a bare word.
exercises.explanation: Swedish says nationality with a bare word after är: Erik är svensk.

mistakes.why: Ett is for ett-words, and läkare is an en-word.

exercises.hint: There is an adjective before the job.
exercises.feedback: With an adjective, the article comes back.
exercises.explanation: A bare profession has no article, but with an adjective it does: en bra läkare.

mistakes.why: That copies the English a. Swedish leaves the article out before a plain profession.

exercises.feedback: English needs a; Swedish does not.
exercises.explanation: After är, a profession stands without an article: min syster är sjuksköterska.

exercises.instruction: Add bra (good) before lärare. Write the whole sentence.

mistakes.why: With an adjective in front of the job, the article is needed again.
Lärare is an en-word, so the -t article does not fit.

exercises.feedback: An adjective brings back the article.
exercises.explanation: A plain profession has no article, but en bra lärare describes what kind of teacher she is, so en comes back.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. The article copies English; Swedish leaves it out before a plain job.
Swapping the article does not help: the job needs no article at all.

exercises.feedback: Compare with English: Swedish has one word fewer.
exercises.explanation: After är, a plain profession has no article: han är läkare.

mistakes.why: That uses the article tile. Swedish leaves the article out before a plain profession.

exercises.feedback: One tile is the English an.
exercises.explanation: A profession after är takes no article: Lars är ingenjör.

mistakes.why: An article is right here because of the adjective, but ingenjör is an en-word, so the -t form does not fit.

exercises.hint: There is an adjective before the job.
exercises.feedback: The adjective brings back the article.
exercises.explanation: With an adjective, a job takes its article again, and ingenjör is an en-word: en duktig ingenjör.
